_about: Hand review of every EU Safety Gate alert in the agreed pilot view -
notified by Germany, Chinese country of origin - over the 12 weekly reports
stored on 2026-09-12 (2026-06-26 to 2026-09-11). todo.md section 2 asked for
15-20; the whole window is only 50, so all 50 are labelled and this measures
precision over the full period rather than a sample.
Labels are the four in todo.md section 2. They decide nothing by themselves:
this file is the evidence behind the routing decision recorded in

29 of the 50 carry more than one measure, so 'measures' is a list and the lag is given for the earliest and the latest; an earlier draft of this file read only the first measure and undercounted marketplace removals as 13.

scope.rule: notifyingCountry = Germany AND countryOfOrigin = People's Republic of China

rules.direct: the alert names J&T Express, or otherwise shows J&T carried the item
rules.customer exposure: the onlineTrader field names a brand with role 'customer' in profile.json (Temu, Shein, AliExpress, TikTok Shop) - the item moved through a platform J&T delivers for
rules.market trend: a Chinese-origin consumer good that German authorities acted on, sold online but not through a key customer; evidence about the goods flow J&T carries, not about a named counterparty
rules.irrelevant: no e-commerce import channel at all, or a channel J&T's business does not touch

findings: direct = 0, and not by chance: no carrier is named in any of the 639 stored alerts. Safety Gate records the product, the brand and the online trader; the carrier is not a field. This is the same structural zero as the DSA database, for the same reason - the duty falls on sellers and platforms.

customer exposure = 20 of 50 (1.7 per week). 15 of these 20 carry the measure 'Removal of this product listing by the online marketplace', i.e. the key customer itself acted. The split is AliExpress 11, Temu 5, Shein 4; TikTok Shop appears in none of the 50 and in 7 alerts notified elsewhere.
The pilot view is all 'Serious risk' (50 of 50), so severity does not rank anything.
Heavy product clustering: 10 of 50 are balloons (chemical), 5 bicycle helmets, 9 adaptors or extension leads, 3 sand-filled toys. The same product class recurs for weeks under different sellers.

Measure-to-publication lag, 47 of 50 alerts carrying an entry-into-force date: median 30 days measured from the earliest measure, 28 from the latest (min 4, max 191); at most 2 of 47 within 7 days. Safety Gate is a retrospective weekly bulletin, so nothing in it can support an immediate alert.

Widening past Germany would add 53 key-customer alerts notified elsewhere (France 29, Luxembourg 10, Ireland 5). Zero of the 53 repeat a product/brand pair already in the German set, so this is not deduplication - it is a different, larger set, and a separate scope question for J&T.
